title: Can geometry teach navigation without target paths?
narration: A scene can support many destinations, but a traversal shows only one route. We ask whether geometric objectives can instead teach a visual policy how to improve a candidate path.
editing_notes: 00:08–00:20. Reveal the scene, then the question. The action-free claim concerns navigation adaptation, not the pretrained VLA backbone.

title: Geometry defines how a path should improve
narration: During training, reconstructed geometry defines an energy that balances goal reaching, progress, obstacle avoidance, heading, and smoothness.
editing_notes: 00:20–00:28. Reveal goal/progress, then obstacle terms, then motion regularity. Energy terms are a formulation; this slide does not claim every term has a nonzero weight in every run.

title: Supervise corrections, not target paths
narration: We query a projection-aware descent direction at the current path. The VLA learns this local correction directly, rather than fitting an optimized target trajectory.
editing_notes: 00:28–00:36. Reveal the oracle arrow first; then reveal the learned model and regression connection. The plotted oracle arrows are cached directions scaled for display, not final projected displacements.

title: Learn on the paths the model visits
narration: Each correction changes the path seen by the next prediction. Dataset aggregation collects oracle labels at these visited paths and retains them across training rounds.
editing_notes: 00:36–00:45. Reveal the four steps left to right, the return arrow, then the replay banks. Initial paths come from the goal-biased unicycle prior. Training collection uses projected energy backtracking; deployment removes this guard.

title: Deployment uses the learned field alone
narration: At deployment, the same learned field repeatedly corrects a candidate path. Only the image, goal, current path, and lightweight kinematic projection are required.
editing_notes: 00:45–00:55. Reveal inputs, model, bounded update, then the feedback arrow. Keep training-only geometry absent. The backbone is pretrained; the recorded example uses adapter-only training.
